note: Structure and guidance written for Cathopedia, following the Order of Mass of the Roman Missal (third edition). The Missal's own texts and rubrics are not reproduced: parts marked "missal" show where the licensed text will appear.
missalPending: The text of this part comes from the Roman Missal. It will appear here once the licensed English Missal is added to Cathopedia.
readingPending: The reading text from an approved Lectionary will appear here once it is licensed. The reference above shows which passage is read today.
readingStudyNote: Text: World English Bible (public domain), for study and preparation. It is not an approved liturgical translation; at Mass, proclaim the reading from an approved Lectionary. Whole verses are shown, so a reading that begins or ends mid-verse may include a few extra words.
homilyPending: Short homily ideas for this day will appear here.

parts.title: Entrance
parts.rubric: As the priest and ministers process to the altar, the Entrance Chant is sung, or the Entrance Antiphon of the day is said. The priest venerates the altar with a kiss and, if incense is used, incenses it, then goes to the chair.

parts.title: Sign of the Cross
parts.rubric: Standing at the chair, the priest and the faithful sign themselves.
parts.text:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
Amen.

parts.title: Greeting
parts.rubric: The priest greets the people with one of the forms given in the Missal; the people reply. He or another minister may briefly introduce the Mass of the day.

parts.title: Penitential Act
parts.rubric: The priest invites the faithful to recall their sins. After a brief silence, one of the forms of the Penitential Act follows, concluded by the priest's absolution. On Sundays, especially in Easter Time, the blessing and sprinkling of water may take its place.

parts.title: Kyrie
parts.rubric: Unless already included in the Penitential Act, the Kyrie invocations follow.
parts.text:
Kyrie, eleison. Kyrie, eleison.
Christe, eleison. Christe, eleison.
Kyrie, eleison. Kyrie, eleison.
parts.textNote: Greek, as in the Missal: Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

parts.title: Gloria
parts.rubric: The Gloria is sung or said today.

parts.title: Collect
parts.rubric: The priest says, "Let us pray," and all pray in silence for a while. Then, with hands extended, he says the Collect of the day; the people conclude with "Amen."

parts.title: First Reading
parts.rubric: All sit. The reader proclaims the first reading from the ambo and ends with the acclamation; the people reply. A brief silence may follow.

parts.title: Responsorial Psalm
parts.rubric: The psalmist or cantor sings or says the verses; the people respond with the refrain.

parts.title: Second Reading
parts.rubric: On Sundays and solemnities a second reading follows, proclaimed as the first.

parts.title: Sequence
parts.rubric: The Sequence of the day is sung before the Alleluia. It is obligatory on Easter Sunday and Pentecost, optional on other days that have one.

parts.title: Gospel Acclamation
parts.rubric: All stand. The Alleluia is sung with its verse, or the verse before the Gospel during Lent, when the Alleluia is not sung.
parts.rubricLent: All stand. During Lent the Alleluia is not sung; the verse before the Gospel is sung with its Lenten acclamation.

parts.title: Gospel
parts.rubric: A deacon asks for and receives the priest's blessing; a priest proclaiming the Gospel himself first prays quietly for worthiness. At the ambo he greets the people, announces the Gospel, signs the book and himself on forehead, lips and breast, may incense the book, and proclaims the Gospel. At the end he kisses the book.

parts.title: Homily
parts.rubric: All sit. The homily is required on Sundays and holydays of obligation and recommended on other days. A brief silence may follow.

parts.title: Profession of Faith
parts.rubric: The Creed is sung or said today. The Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed is used; the Apostles' Creed may be used instead, especially in Lent and Easter Time. All bow at the words about the Incarnation, and genuflect on the solemnities of the Annunciation and the Nativity of the Lord.

parts.title: Universal Prayer
parts.who: Priest, deacon or reader, and people
parts.rubric: The priest introduces the Prayer of the Faithful from the chair. Intentions are announced for the Church, for public authorities and the salvation of the world, for those in any need, and for the local community; the people respond after each. The priest concludes with a prayer.

parts.title: Preparation of the Gifts
parts.rubric: The altar is prepared and the gifts are brought forward while the Offertory Chant is sung. The priest offers the bread and the wine with their prayers, mixes a little water with the wine, washes his hands, and invites the people to pray; they respond.
parts.missal: Prayers at the preparation of the gifts

parts.title: Prayer over the Offerings
parts.rubric: With hands extended, the priest says the Prayer over the Offerings of the day; the people reply, "Amen."
parts.missal: Prayer over the Offerings of the day

parts.title: Preface
parts.rubric: The Eucharistic Prayer begins with the dialogue and the Preface. Choose the Preface proper to the day or the season.

parts.title: Holy, Holy, Holy
parts.rubric: At the end of the Preface, all sing or say the Sanctus. The people kneel after it, where that is the custom.

parts.title: Eucharistic Prayer
parts.rubric: The priest says one of the Eucharistic Prayers. The consecration follows the Institution Narrative: he shows the consecrated host and the chalice to the people and genuflects after each. After the Mystery of Faith, the prayer continues to the concluding doxology, to which the people reply, "Amen."

parts.title: The Lord's Prayer
parts.rubric: All stand. After the priest's introduction, all say or sing the Lord's Prayer together. The priest continues alone with the embolism, and the people conclude with the doxology.
parts.text:
Our Father, who art in heaven,
hallowed be thy name;
thy kingdom come,
thy will be done
on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us this day our daily bread,
and forgive us our trespasses,
as we forgive those who trespass against us;
and lead us not into temptation,
but deliver us from evil.

parts.title: Sign of Peace
parts.rubric: The priest says the prayer for peace and greets the people with the peace of the Lord. The deacon or priest may invite all to offer one another a sign of peace.

parts.title: Lamb of God
parts.rubric: While the Agnus Dei is sung or said, the priest breaks the host and places a small piece in the chalice. He then prays quietly in preparation for Communion.
parts.missal: Agnus Dei and the priest's private prayer

parts.title: Communion
parts.rubric: The priest genuflects, shows the host to the people and, with them, makes the response before Communion. He receives Communion, then distributes it. The Communion Chant is sung, or the Communion Antiphon is said. Afterwards the vessels are purified and a period of silence may be kept.

parts.title: Prayer after Communion
parts.rubric: Standing at the altar or the chair, the priest says, "Let us pray," and the Prayer after Communion of the day; the people reply, "Amen."
parts.missal: Prayer after Communion of the day

parts.title: Announcements
parts.rubric: Brief announcements, if any, are made now.

parts.title: Blessing
parts.rubric: The priest greets the people and blesses them. On certain days or occasions a Solemn Blessing or a Prayer over the People may be used.

parts.title: Dismissal
parts.rubric: The deacon, or the priest, dismisses the people with one of the formulas in the Missal; the people reply, "Thanks be to God." During the Octave of Easter and on Pentecost a double Alleluia is added. The priest venerates the altar with a kiss and, after a profound bow with the ministers, withdraws.

goodFriday: There is no Mass on Good Friday. The Celebration of the Passion of the Lord follows its own order: the Liturgy of the Word, the Adoration of the Holy Cross, and Holy Communion. The readings of the day are shown below.
holySaturday: On Holy Saturday the Church waits at the Lord's tomb, and the Sacrifice of the Mass is not celebrated until the Easter Vigil after nightfall.
